# Numora

Numora is a framework-agnostic numeric input and number input library for JavaScript and React. It solves the fundamental problems with `<input type="number">` - cursor jumping, scientific notation leaking, paste chaos, mobile keyboard issues, and locale-specific decimal/thousand separator conflicts.

## Packages

- **numora** (vanilla JS / any framework): https://www.npmjs.com/package/numora
- **numora-react** (React wrapper): https://www.npmjs.com/package/numora-react

## API Reference - numora (vanilla JS)

All values are strings; Numora never converts them to `Number`. The raw value is canonical in
every locale: ASCII digits, `.` decimal, no grouping (a de-DE field showing `1.234,5` reports
`1234.5`).

```ts
import { NumoraInput, FormatOn, GroupingStyle } from 'numora'

// The first argument is an existing <input> (Numora adopts it) or a container element
// (Numora creates the <input> inside it).
const numoraInput = new NumoraInput(inputOrContainerElement, {
  decimalMaxLength?: number,          // max decimal places (default 18)
  decimalMinLength?: number,          // min decimal places, pads zeros on blur (default 0)
  thousandSeparator?: string,         // default ','
  groupingStyle?: GroupingStyle,      // 'thousand' (default) | 'lakh' | 'wan' | 'none'
  decimalSeparator?: string,          // default '.'
  formatOn?: FormatOn,                // FormatOn.Change (default) | FormatOn.Blur
  locale?: string | boolean,          // e.g. 'de-DE', or true for the browser locale
  allowCompactNotation?: boolean,     // '1k' -> '1000'
  allowScientificNotation?: boolean,  // default true: pasted '1.5e-7' -> '0.00000015'; false: rejected
  allowNegative?: boolean,
  allowLeadingZeros?: boolean,
  padLeadingZero?: boolean,           // '.5' -> '0.5'
  maxLength?: number,                 // raw length; separators not counted
  isAllowed?: (rawValue: string) => boolean, // reject a user edit by returning false
  onValueChange?: ({ value, formattedValue }) => void, // fires when the raw value changes
  onFormattedValueChange?: (formattedValue: string) => void, // fires on every rewrite of the text
  defaultValue?: string,              // canonical raw value
  // native attributes: id, name, className, placeholder, disabled, readOnly, required,
  // tabIndex, title, autofocus, ariaLabel
})

numoraInput.rawValue            // raw, e.g. '1234.5'
numoraInput.formattedValue      // displayed, e.g. '1,234.5'
numoraInput.element             // the <input>
numoraInput.setValue('1234.5')  // does not call onValueChange or isAllowed
numoraInput.update({ decimalMaxLength: 2 }) // merges over the current options; a key you leave out keeps its value
numoraInput.destroy()           // remove Numora's listeners
```

Values the app passes in (`defaultValue`, `setValue`) always expand scientific notation,
even with `allowScientificNotation: false`, since `String(1e21)` is `'1e+21'`.

Format or parse without an input (both packages export these):

```ts
import { formatValue, parseValue, getSeparatorsFromLocale } from 'numora'

formatValue('1234.5', { locale: 'de-DE', decimalMinLength: 2 }) // '1.234,50'
parseValue('1.234,50', { locale: 'de-DE' })                      // '1234.50'
getSeparatorsFromLocale('de-DE') // the locale's thousand and decimal separators and grouping style
```

The v4 names (`enableNegative`, `enableLeadingZeros`, `enableCompactNotation`,
`autoAddLeadingZero`, `maxDecimals`, `thousandStyle`, `rawValueMode`,
`enableScientificNotation`, `emitRawValue`, vanilla `value` and `onChange`) are removed in v5: they are ignored with a development warning.

`numora/pipeline` exports the single sanitization steps, with no semver
guarantee. `numora/internal` is for `numora-react` only; do not import it.

## API Reference - numora-react

```tsx
import { NumoraInput, FormatOn, GroupingStyle } from 'numora-react'

<NumoraInput
  decimalMaxLength={2}
  groupingStyle={GroupingStyle.Thousand}
  formatOn={FormatOn.Change}
  locale="de-DE"
  allowNegative
  value={amount}               // canonical raw value, e.g. "1234.56"
  onChange={(e) => {
    e.target.value             // raw value, e.g. "1234.56"
    e.target.formattedValue    // displayed string, e.g. "1.234,56"
  }}
  onValueChange={({ value, formattedValue }) => {}}  // same payload as vanilla
  onFormattedValueChange={(formattedValue) => {}}    // every rewrite of the text
/>
```

Use `defaultValue` instead of `value` for an uncontrolled field. A ref typed as
`NumoraHTMLInputElement` has `rawValue`, `formattedValue` and `setValue(value)`.

## Common Use Cases

- **DeFi / financial inputs**: keep large and tiny values in decimal notation, enforce decimal precision, expose raw value for smart contract calls
- **International forms**: locale-aware decimal and thousand separators (e.g. German `1.234,56`)
- **React Hook Form integration**: use `Controller` and pass `e.target.value` (the raw value) to `field.onChange`; `register` is not supported
- **Mobile-safe inputs**: normalises mobile keyboard quirks across iOS and Android
- **Formatted display while typing**: thousand separators added live without breaking cursor position
